info-01-c1.text: C. E. Shannon (1948). A Mathematical Theory of Communication. Bell System Technical Journal 27.
info-01-c1.quote: If the base 2 is used the resulting units may be called binary digits, or more briefly bits, a word suggested by J. W. Tukey.
info-01-c1.claim: The base-2 logarithm gives bits, which are yes/no answers.

info-01-c3.text: C. E. Shannon (1948). A Mathematical Theory of Communication. Bell System Technical Journal 27.
info-01-c3.quote: The uncertainty of y is never increased by knowledge of x. It will be decreased unless x and y are independent events, in which case it is not changed.
info-01-c3.claim: Conditioning never increases entropy: H(Y|X) ≤ H(Y).

info-01-c3.text: C. E. Shannon (1948). A Mathematical Theory of Communication. Bell System Technical Journal 27.
info-01-c3.quote: It will be decreased unless x and y are independent events, in which case it is not changed.
info-01-c3.claim: Equality holds exactly when X and Y are independent, that is, when knowing X is useless.
